claim.quote: An excess of events is observed, with a significance of 5.2 standard deviations, over the expectation from the background-only hypothesis.

date.note: arXiv submission date; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 120, 231801 (2018)

name: Observation of ttH production

summary.plain: CMS observed Higgs bosons produced together with a top quark and an anti-top quark. The paper explains that on-shell top quarks are too heavy to appear in Higgs boson decays, so this production process is how the Higgs boson's coupling to the top quark can be constrained.
summary.technical: Combination of ttH searches in WW, ZZ, γγ, ττ and bb final states at 7, 8 and 13 TeV (up to 5.1, 19.7 and 35.9 fb⁻¹): 5.2σ observed, 4.2σ expected, signal strength 1.26 +0.31 -0.26.

title: Observation of ttH production
why_it_matters: In the Standard Model the masses of elementary fermions are accounted for by Yukawa interactions, with a coupling proportional to the fermion mass. The paper says the top-quark Yukawa coupling cannot be tested from a decay rate, so constraints come from pp → ttH production; the combined best-fit signal strength normalised to the standard model prediction is 1.26 +0.31/−0.26.
